about.title: Personal Injury Help in Yreka, California
about.longDescription: Yreka may be a small city, but its roads still see their share of collisions. Public records show 9 injury collisions in the most recent reporting year, with 13 people hurt — a reminder that even a quiet community isn't immune to crashes. Local corridors like Interstate 5 (both directions), Rt 3, and S Main Street see the most reported collision activity, likely reflecting the traffic these routes carry through town. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and missed work can feel overwhelming on top of physical recovery. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Yreka with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we don't decide your case or charge you anything. Attorneys in our network handle cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Our goal is simply to make that first connection easier so you can focus on healing while someone with legal experience looks at what happened and what your options might be.

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California law generally gives you two years from the date of an injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Acting sooner helps preserve evidence and options.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened — your share of fault simply reduces the amount, it doesn't eliminate your claim.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on compensation for things like pain and suffering, unlike some states that cap these damages.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover money on your behalf — so there's no fee to speak with someone about your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Yreka?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a lawsuit for most personal injury claims. If a government entity was involved, such as a city vehicle or road defect, the notice deadline can be as short as six months. It's best to look into your options as early as possible.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Any amount you're awarded would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but you can still pursue a claim.

items.question: Where do collisions tend to cluster in Yreka?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along Interstate 5 (both southbound and northbound), Rt 3, and S Main Street. These are simply the corridors with the most reported incidents, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney — we're not a law firm and don't charge you anything. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they only get paid if they win or settle your case.

items.question: Does it matter what day or time my accident happened?
items.answer: Not for your legal rights, but it can help establish the circumstances of what happened. In Yreka, reported crashes tend to cluster around Tuesday afternoons between noon and 2 p.m., which may be useful context when reconstructing events.
